time-tracker.title: MCP Time Tracker

time-tracker.example: "Start a timer for Acme, task: API refactor" ... "Stop it and show me this week's hours per project with amounts."
time-tracker.free: Unlimited timers and entries; reports, lists and CSV cover the last 7 days; 2 projects with rates. Currency per entry (EUR, USD, GBP, PLN).
time-tracker.pro: Full history, invoice_summary, group by tag, unlimited rated projects.

price-tracker.title: MCP Price Tracker
price-tracker.tagline: Check and watch product prices on ordinary shop pages.

Stores watches with a price history, refreshes them, computes min, max and change, and flags target hits and drops of 5% or more. Manual entry covers pages that block bots.
price-tracker.for: Anyone who asks their assistant what something costs now, whether it dropped, or to keep an eye on it.
price-tracker.example: "What does this laptop cost right now?" ... "Watch it and tell me when it drops under 900."
price-tracker.free: Unlimited price checks with extraction confidence; 3 watches with 30 observations each; alerts_pending free; redirects off product pages are refused.
price-tracker.pro: Unlimited watches, full history, refresh all.

spreadsheet.title: MCP Spreadsheet
spreadsheet.tagline: Read, query, edit and convert xlsx and csv files safely.
spreadsheet.does: Opens xlsx, xlsm, xlsb, ods, csv and tsv files, guesses the header row on messy exports, sniffs delimiters, and answers questions with a safe expression language (no eval): filters, sorts, per-column stats, find, computed columns such as [Qty] * [Unit Price], and conversion between formats. It never overwrites the source unless told to.
spreadsheet.for: Anyone who says: open this file, tell me what is in it, filter it, add a column, save it.
spreadsheet.example: "Open orders.xlsx and show open orders over 5 units sorted by amount" ... "Add a Total column and save as CSV."
spreadsheet.free: Read, query (filters, group by, sum/avg/min/max), stats and find on files up to 5,000 rows; writes up to 500 rows, never a partial file above that.
spreadsheet.storage: Works on the user's own files; nothing else stored.

invoice.title: MCP Invoice
invoice.tagline: Numbered invoices with tax lines, rendered to a professional PDF.
invoice.does: Stores the issuer profile and clients, allocates invoice numbers that never repeat (INV-YYYY-NNNN), computes per-line rounding, multiple VAT rates and discounts in integer minor units, renders an A4 PDF with pdfkit (multi-page tables, totals, payment details), tracks paid status and reports overdue invoices. Pairs with the time tracker: hours become an invoice in the same chat.
invoice.for: Freelancers and small businesses that want to say: make an invoice for Acme, 12 hours at 90 EUR, due in 14 days.
invoice.example: "Invoice Acme for 12 h at 90 EUR with 23% VAT, due in 14 days, and give me the PDF."
invoice.free: 3 invoices per calendar month; overdue report free; PDF carries a small footer line.
invoice.pro: Unlimited invoices, no branding, logo, custom prefix.

expense-tracker.title: MCP Expense Tracker
expense-tracker.tagline: Receipts, mileage and expenses that turn into invoice lines.
expense-tracker.does: Logs expenses with per-expense currency, VAT split and receipt attachment (path + sha256), auto-categorises merchants by rules, records mileage with country rate tables, summarises by category, project, month or merchant per currency, exports CSV or xlsx, and emits invoice-ready line items (net + tax rate, so nothing is taxed twice) for rebilling a project with optional markup.
expense-tracker.for: Freelancers and small businesses who already track time and invoice from chat and want the receipts side closed in the same place.
expense-tracker.example: "I paid 61.50 EUR at Media Markt for a USB hub, Acme project, billable" ... "Give me the invoice lines to rebill Acme this month with 10% markup."

expense-tracker.pro: Full history, unlimited projects and rules, xlsx export, unlimited rebill items with markup.

office-suite.title: MCP Office Suite (bundle server)

office-suite.for: Anyone who wants the whole freelancer workflow in one config line.
office-suite.example: "Start a timer for Acme" ... "Invoice Acme for this week's hours plus the USB hub receipt."
office-suite.pro: The $39 bundle key unlocks every child.

currency.title: MCP Currency Converter
currency.tagline: ECB reference rates: convert, history, and fx_rates for rebilling.
currency.does: Fetches and caches the European Central Bank daily and historical reference rates (keyless, free), converts any amount between currencies via EUR cross rates with the rate date stated, returns history tables with min, max and average, and emits the exact fx_rates object the expense tracker needs to rebill a project in one currency, so a model can chain the two without the user supplying rates.

quotes.free: 5 open quotes at a time, unlimited pasteable text quotes, accept, decline, revise, VAT, discounts and multi-currency, pipeline and win-rate report for the current calendar year to date.

zip.pro: Unlimited archives, no size cap and no entry cap.

billing-docs.title: MCP Billing Docs
billing-docs.tagline: Credit notes and purchase orders, on the same engine as your invoices.
billing-docs.does: Writes credit notes against the invoices the mcp-invoice server already holds, in full, by gross amount or by named lines and quantities, with every money field stored negative in minor units so a period's documents sum to the net of what was billed; a credit note by amount splits that gross across the VAT rates the invoice actually used, and no credit note can ever give back more than the invoice's remaining creditable amount. It also raises purchase orders to suppliers with line items, VAT, currency and an expected delivery date, receives them in full or in part, and reports credited and on-order totals per currency alongside deliveries past their date.
billing-docs.for: Anyone who invoices clients and has to reverse one, and anyone who orders from suppliers and needs the order on paper.
billing-docs.example: "Credit invoice INV-2026-0001 in full, the client returned the work." ... "Credit 177 euro of that invoice, they were overcharged." ... "Raise a purchase order to Nordic Print for 500 brochures at 1.20 each, due the 20th." ... "Which orders are past their delivery date?"
billing-docs.free: 5 documents per calendar month, credit notes and purchase orders together, counted by issue date, with full, partial and per-line credit notes, VAT, multiple currencies and receiving orders all included, and both text exports never metered.
billing-docs.pro: Unlimited documents, both A4 PDFs with your logo and no footer credit, and the billing_docs_report of credited, on-order and overdue deliveries.

deposits.title: MCP Deposits
deposits.tagline: Security and retainer deposits, held per client, on the same engine as your invoices.
deposits.does: Records a security or retainer deposit when the money arrives, in minor units and in the currency it arrived in, and then answers for it: what is held per client and per currency, since when, and what has already gone. Applying a deposit to an invoice writes the payment onto that invoice under both locks, adding to what was already paid rather than replacing it, so a bank transfer that landed first is not erased; it can never pay out more than the deposit still holds or more than the invoice still owes, and a deposit is never converted between currencies. Refunds hand money back without touching the invoice, the stored status is derived from the movements every time one is written, and the statement is one client in one currency, as text or as an A4 PDF that matches the invoice and credit note next to it.
deposits.for: Anyone who takes money before the work: landlords and letting agents on security deposits, agencies and consultants on retainers, trades on up-front payments.
deposits.example: "Record a 500 euro security deposit from Nordic Print, received today." ... "Apply 300 of that deposit to INV-2026-0001." ... "How much are we holding for Nordic Print?" ... "Refund the rest, paid back by bank transfer."
deposits.free: 5 deposits recorded per calendar month, counted by received date, with applying to invoices, refunds, lists, balances and the text statement all unlimited on every tier: a cap that trapped a client's deposit would be a limit on their money rather than on yours.
deposits.pro: Unlimited deposits recorded, the A4 deposit statement PDF with your logo and no footer credit, and the deposits_report of held per currency, oldest held and what has sat unapplied.

per-diem.title: MCP Per Diem
per-diem.tagline: Statutory travel allowances on the rate tables the tax authorities publish, and the trips you priced with them.
per-diem.does: Prices one business trip against a bundled rate table and shows the arithmetic: the allowance per day, the partial-day fraction the scheme's own ladder produced, every deduction for a meal somebody else paid for, and the total in the scheme's own currency. Three schemes ship with it: the Polish delegation regulation at home and per country, the HMRC benchmark scale rates for travel inside the UK, and the US GSA CONUS standard M&IE with the lodging cap. Start and end are instants rather than wall clocks, so a trip across a clock change is 23 or 25 hours and the Polish 24-hour period and the US calendar day give different, correct answers to the same trip. Trips can be saved under a name with a TRIP-YYYY-NNNN id, listed with a total per currency, reported per scheme and per month, and handed to the expense tracker as ready-made expense_add arguments. The tables are files inside the package, not a feed, so the same trip priced twice gives the same answer, and every rate carries its authority, instrument, source URL and effective date.
per-diem.for: Anyone who claims or pays a statutory travel allowance: Polish contractors and employers on delegacja and diety, UK sole traders and companies on the HMRC benchmark rates, and US federal or corporate travellers on the GSA standard.
per-diem.example: "What is the per diem for 58 hours in Krakow, leaving Tuesday 8am, with breakfast on the first day and two nights in a hotel?" ... "Same trip under the HMRC rates." ... "Save it as the Krakow audit trip." ... "Total my per diems this quarter per scheme."
per-diem.free: Rate lookups and calculations are unlimited on every tier: the tables are public regulation, and metering the reading of a regulation would be charging for the tax authority's work. 5 trips saved per calendar month, counted by start date, and unlimited trip lists.
per-diem.pro: Unlimited trips saved, the expense-tracker export payloads (one per currency, ready for expense_add), and the report of totals per scheme and per calendar month.

asset-register.title: MCP Asset Register
asset-register.tagline: A fixed asset register that depreciates on the rates the tax authorities actually publish, with the schedule, the journal and the gain on sale.
asset-register.does: Keeps a register of what you bought, what it cost, when it went into use and which category it falls in, and returns the rate, the useful life, the convention, the full schedule year by year or month by month, one month's journal entry, and the gain or loss when you sell. Three tables ship with it: the Polish annual rates from the annex to the CIT and PIT acts keyed to the KST classification (33 rows, with declining-balance eligibility and the art. 16k switch to straight line), the UK capital allowance pools at 18 and 6 percent with the annual investment allowance, and the US MACRS GDS half-year percentages for 3, 5 and 7 year property exactly as IRS Pub 946 Table A-1 publishes them. The convention is the table's, not the caller's: Poland charges from the month AFTER the asset enters the register, so an asset in service on 15 March starts on 1 April and year one is nine twelfths, while the MACRS percentages already carry the half-year convention and a UK writing down allowance is not prorated by month at all. The same asset gives three different year-one figures under the three schemes and all three are right. Money is integer minor units end to end and the schedule is allocated by cumulative rounding, so the periods sum to cost less residual to the minor unit and the months sum to their year. The tables are files inside the package, not a feed, and every rate carries its authority, instrument, source URL and effective date.
asset-register.for: Anyone who has to put a depreciation figure on a return or in a ledger: Polish companies and sole traders on the KST annex rates, UK businesses claiming capital allowances on the main and special rate pools, and US filers on MACRS GDS.
asset-register.example: "Add the Dell workstation, 8,499 zloty, in service 15 March 2026, computers." ... "Show me the schedule month by month." ... "Depreciate the same truck under declining balance." ... "What is April's journal entry?" ... "We sold the van for 12,000 in September, what is the gain?"
asset-register.free: Depreciation schedules are unlimited on every tier: the rates are public information a tax authority published, and metering the reading of a regulation would be charging for the government's work. The cap is on the SIZE of the register, 10 assets, plus unlimited asset_list and asset_dispose.
asset-register.pro: Unlimited assets in the register, the monthly journal entry with its ready-made expense_add payload (one per currency, no vat_rate because depreciation is a book charge), and the report of net book value by category and currency with the year's charge and every disposal in it.

statement-of-account.title: MCP Statement of Account
statement-of-account.tagline: The one document that answers what a client actually owes you, aged as at any date, with the chaser drafted.
statement-of-account.does: Reads the three books this suite already keeps -- the invoice ledger, the credit notes and the deposits -- and turns them into a statement of account for a period: the balance carried at the start, every invoice issued, every payment received, every credit note given, the deposits applied broken out of the receipts rather than added again, and the closing balance. The movements are in date order and the opening balance plus their sum equals the closing balance, so the document is auditable line by line. statement_aging splits what is still open into 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days past the due date AS AT the date asked for, which means an invoice issued after that date is not on the books, a payment made after it has not happened and a credit note issued after it has not been given. Due today is not overdue: day zero sits in a not-yet-due line reported beside the four buckets. paid_minor on the invoice is the authority and the payment rows are only the attribution, so a deposit application that raised paid_minor without writing a payment row still appears. It writes into no book it reports on: bytes and mtimes of the sibling stores are unchanged across all six tools, and the only file it owns is a register of the statements it built. Nothing here invents a late fee, an interest rate or a legal cost, and a dunning letter escalates in tone and never in figures.
statement-of-account.for: Anyone who invoices and then has to chase: freelancers and small firms who need to send a client a statement rather than forwarding five invoices, and anyone who has to answer what was owed on a given date rather than what is owed now.
statement-of-account.example: "Send Acme a statement for June." ... "Who owes me money, aged." ... "What was outstanding on 10 June?" ... "Draft a firm chaser for Acme." ... "Show me every client, per currency, with the oldest overdue invoice."
statement-of-account.free: statement_aging is free and unlimited on every tier, for one client or for everyone: who owes me money is the question this server exists for, and a free tier that hides it is a demo. The meter is on the document that goes to a client, five distinct statements a calendar month, counted by client, period and currency, so rebuilding one already in the register is free forever. Plain-text statements and dunning at the friendly and firm levels are free.
statement-of-account.pro: Unlimited statements, the A4 PDF on the same page layout as your invoices with your logo and no footer credit, the level 3 final demand, and statements_report: every client at once, totalled per currency, ranked by what is overdue rather than by what is large, with the oldest overdue invoice in the whole book named.

cash-book.title: MCP Cash Book
cash-book.tagline: One double-entry ledger derived from the books you already keep, proved to the minor unit.
cash-book.does: Reads six sibling stores read-only -- the invoice ledger, the credit note and purchase order store, the deposit store, the expense ledger, the bank import and the fixed asset register -- and derives a debit and a credit for every movement in a period. Revenue and VAT output come off the invoices, receivables and the payments that clear them, deposits held as the liability they are, expenses by category with the VAT taken OUT of the gross rather than added on top, fixed assets entering service, and depreciation charged by month. The bank import posts nothing: a bank line and a payment record are one transaction seen twice, so cash is posted from the documents and each bank row is matched to a posted cash movement of the same amount, the same direction and a date within three days, as evidence written onto the line as bank_ref. What is left over is the output that matters, because a bank debit with no expense behind it is a payment nobody entered. Nothing is ever balanced with a plug: an entry whose own legs do not add up is posted exactly as the document states it and the difference is raised by name, with the entry, the source server and the source document behind every unit of it. Currencies are never added together, a purchase order is a memo that is never posted, a deposit applied to an invoice moves the liability rather than cash, and the ledger opens at nothing because an opening figure nobody can walk back to a document is the first invented number in a set of books. Every line carries the server, the document id and the ISO date it came from, and no sibling store changes bytes or mtime across any of the six tools.
cash-book.for: Anyone running this suite who has to answer whether the books add up, and anyone who has to hand an accountant a ledger rather than six exports: freelancers and small firms at month end, and bookkeepers who need every figure to name the document it came from.
cash-book.example: "Build the ledger for June." ... "Does June balance?" ... "Show me every line hitting receivables." ... "Close June and tell me what is unposted." ... "Export the June ledger as CSV."
cash-book.free: trial_balance and ledger_lines are free and unlimited on every tier: whether the books add up is the question this server exists for, and a free tier that hides the answer is a demo. The meter is on the PERIOD, three distinct periods a calendar month, keyed by from, to and currency, so rebuilding one already in the register is free forever on every tier.
cash-book.pro: Unlimited periods, month_close with its trial balance snapshot and its list of what the month leaves unposted or inconsistent, ledger_export_csv as RFC 4180 text with no file written, and ledger_report with the movement and closing balance per account plus the purchase commitments held as a memo.

This server is not that shape and a comparison page would be dishonest about which one a reader wants: it posts nothing, it stores no book of its own beyond a register of the periods it built, and it derives the whole ledger on the call from six local stores it never writes to. The comparison a reader would actually want is against a spreadsheet, and the measured result of that comparison is the guide /guides/one-ledger-from-every-server rather than a table.
